synopsis: SLAM is one of three approaches presented for measuring real sites in three dimensions, using a moving machine’s own sensors rather than overlapping photographs or laser distance measurements [f13133]. The booklet treats it as a method in its own right because a large installed fleet can supply recordings for site-model acquisition [f13140]. Machine-log reconstruction using classical SLAM, SfM and meshing requires synchronised cameras, lidar, IMU and GNSS, together with calibration [f4216]. A key limitation is visibility bias in forward-facing route logs: they do not observe stockpile backs or upper surfaces that a taller future sensor could see, leaving gaps in the reconstructed site [f13141].

relations.note: Specifies sensor synchronisation and calibration requirements for turning fleet recordings into site models.
Explains the fleet-acquisition rationale for treating SLAM as a distinct site-measurement method.
Adds a route-log visibility limitation to the machine-log reconstruction workflow.
Qualifies fleet-based acquisition: forward-facing recordings leave some site surfaces unobserved.
